items.title: 63 countries eliminate at least one neglected tropical disease as WHO reports global progress
items.description: The number of countries that have eliminated at least one neglected tropical disease (NTD) has increased to 63, up from 42 at the end of 2020, according to the World Health Organisation (WHO). The development represents significant progress in global efforts to control and eliminate diseases that disproportionately affect the world’s poorest and most vulnerable communities. However, WHO says these gains remain fragile, with inadequate funding, gaps in disease surveillance, and uneven progress threatening efforts to meet the 2030 targets. These findings are contained in the Global Report on Neglected Tropical Diseases 2026, which provides a midterm assessment of the implementation of the WHO 2021–2030 road map. The report indicates that the number of people requiring interventions against NTDs fell to 1.41 billion in 2024, representing a 36 per cent reduction since 2010 and a 19 per cent decline since 2020. It also highlights major improvements in controlling some diseases. Cases of sleeping sickness, also known as human African trypanosomiasis, have declined by 98 per cent since 1999, while Guinea worm disease recorded just 10 human cases in 2025, its lowest level on record. Despite these achievements, WHO warns that sustaining the progress will require stronger government commitment, increased domestic financing and continued support from international development partners. WHO Director-General warns against losing progress WHO Director-General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus described the elimination of neglected tropical diseases as a major success story in global health. However, he cautioned that the progress made over the years could be reversed without sustained investment and stronger health systems. “Elimination of neglected tropical diseases is one of the standout success stories of global health,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General. “However, the hard-won gains we have made could easily be lost, so countries and partners must step up, not step back, by increasing domestic financing, sustaining external support and integrating NTD services into primary health care,” saying the goal is not only to eliminate diseases, but to free communities from disability, disfigurement, death and generational poverty. Scientific advances provide new treatment options The report also identifies advances in science and medicine that are providing new opportunities to prevent and treat neglected tropical diseases. Among these developments is the WHO prequalification of child-friendly praziquantel to treat schistosomiasis. Other advances include the availability of generic miltefosine for leishmaniasis and a dengue vaccine. In addition, two chikungunya vaccines and new medicines for onchocerciasis and human African trypanosomiasis have received regulatory approval. These developments are expected to strengthen the range of tools available for disease prevention and treatment. However, WHO says scientific progress alone will not be enough to meet global targets, particularly where health systems lack the resources and capacity to deliver interventions effectively. Rising dengue cases and gaps in disease control Although the report records substantial progress against several NTDs, it also highlights areas where global efforts are falling behind. Dengue cases reached a record 15.1 million in 2024, while deaths from vector-borne neglected tropical diseases have increased. Efforts to eradicate yaws are also off track. The report also finds that only three disease-specific indicators met their 2025 milestones, underscoring the difficulty of achieving targets set under the 2021–2030 road map. WHO also identifies weaknesses in disease data collection and reporting as a major challenge. Gaps in comprehensive, timely information, including gender-disaggregated data, make it difficult to accurately assess progress and identify populations that need targeted interventions. The situation raises concerns about countries’ ability to monitor disease trends and measure intervention effectiveness. Funding shortages threaten disease control programmes One major concern highlighted in the report is the continued dependence of neglected tropical disease programmes on international development assistance. Between 2018 and 2024, a small number of donors provided nearly 80 per cent of international development assistance for NTDs. WHO warns that this concentration has made programmes particularly vulnerable to sudden reductions in financial support. These funding disruptions have affected mass treatment campaigns, case management, disease surveillance, and vector control activities. They have also increased the risk that donated medicines will expire because programmes no longer have enough resources to distribute them. Overall, resources available for neglected tropical diseases remain 30 per cent below pre-COVID-19 levels, with dedicated funding for some programmes having almost disappeared. The funding situation poses a significant challenge for countries that depend on external assistance to sustain disease prevention, treatment, and elimination activities. Countries adopt integrated approaches to disease control Despite the financial challenges, WHO says several countries are taking steps to make their NTD programmes more sustainable. More countries where neglected tropical diseases are prevalent are incorporating interventions into national health strategies, essential health service packages and domestic budgets. There is also growing emphasis on delivering interventions for multiple diseases through shared health services rather than operating separate programmes for each disease. One example is the WHO-recommended integrated strategy for skin-related neglected tropical diseases. The approach is intended to improve efficiency by bringing interventions for different diseases together through shared services. Such integration is also expected to strengthen health service delivery and make better use of available resources. WHO calls for accelerated action before 2030 With five years remaining before the 2030 deadline, WHO says countries and development partners must accelerate efforts to protect the progress already achieved and address persistent gaps. The organisation is calling on countries affected by neglected tropical diseases to increase domestic financing and incorporate NTD interventions into universal health coverage. It also urges governments to adapt disease control programmes to changing circumstances, including conflict and climate change. Donors are being encouraged to broaden their financial support across different NTD interventions rather than concentrating assistance on a limited number of programmes. Recipient countries are also being asked to diversify their funding sources to reduce dependence on a small number of international development partners. The report recognises considerable progress despite limited resources, but stresses that stronger, sustained action will be necessary to meet the 2030 targets.

items.title: Dr Alanky commissions GH¢1.8m classroom block for Falahia Islamic Primary School, announces scholarships
items.description: Businessman and owner of Fanko Hospitality Hotel, Dr Alhaj Nurideen Froko Alanky, has commissioned a six-unit classroom block with ancillary facilities for Falahia Islamic Primary School. The project, which cost more than GH¢1.8 million, is expected to improve teaching and learning conditions at the school. Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, Dr Alanky described education as the bedrock of human civilisation and paid tribute to the founders of the school, whom he commended as men of faith and wisdom for establishing the institution despite their limited resources. He said the project was intended to immortalise the founders and help restore the school’s former standing, stressing that traditional schools such as Falahia had a rich history and identity that deserved to be preserved and supported. Dr Alanky urged teachers to remain vigilant in their role as guardians of children and called on parents to visit the school regularly, work closely with teachers and ensure that their wards complied with the school’s rules and regulations. He also appealed to the Parent-Teacher Association (PTA), the Old Boys Association and his colleagues to support the school to sustain its development. He expressed gratitude to his family, the project team led by his friend, Samshsadeen Issa, and the project chairman for their contributions towards the successful completion of the facility. As part of his support for the school, Dr Alanky announced a scholarship scheme under his Foundation for the first 10 students who obtain aggregate scores of between 9 and 12 in the Junior Secondary School (JSS) examination. He said the Foundation would cover the beneficiaries’ first-year school accessories and all expenses required to enable them to enrol and attend school. Dr Alanky said the commissioning of the classroom block marked the beginning of a broader commitment to the development of the school, adding that the project would not be his last intervention.

items.title: UN and global health leaders declare climate change a health pandemic as 2026 temperatures hit record highs
items.description: Global climate leaders and meteorological authorities declared on November 9, 2026, that relentless greenhouse gas emissions and an “off-the-charts” El Niño event have officially transformed the climate emergency into a global health crisis of pandemic proportions. Speaking at a joint World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) press conference convened during COP31 in Antalya, representatives from the United Nations and global health philanthropies warned that rising temperatures, ocean heating, and unprecedented drought are severely straining health systems, threatening food security, and driving millions of premature deaths worldwide. WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo’s State of the Climate Update 2026 confirms that global temperatures have breached critical thresholds. From January to September 2026, the global average temperature stood approximately 1.47 °C above pre-industrial baselines. The update confirms that the past 12 years are the warmest 12-year period ever recorded, and that the past four years—including 2026—rank among the four hottest years in human history. WMO forecasts indicate that sea-surface temperatures in the Tropical Pacific—the epicentre of El Niño—are expected to reach nearly four times the standard 0.5 °C El Niño threshold between November 2026 and January 2027. Secretary-General Saulo emphasised that because El Niño traditionally exerts its maximum influence on atmospheric temperatures in the year after its initial development, 2027 is projected to break global temperature records again, following the record set during the 2024 El Niño cycle. Beyond rising air temperatures, ocean heat reached its highest level on record for the tenth consecutive year, while global sea levels hit new highs, compounding storm surge and flooding risks for roughly 900 million residents living along low-lying coastal zones worldwide. Extreme weather events intensified across every region in 2026, including high-mountain disasters in China and Nepal that threatened downstream communities, devastating floods in parts of South America and Africa, and severe droughts across Central America, Asia, and the Pacific. Heat mortality, drought, and maternal vulnerability UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell framed the environmental indicators in stark medical terms, warning that climate destruction is directly destabilising human physiology and national health infrastructures. He highlighted severe health impacts documented during the northern summer of 2026, where extreme heat waves led to an estimated 50,000 excess deaths across Europe alongside dangerous heat spikes across India, Pakistan, and North America. “The climate crisis is now a global health crisis of pandemic proportions. From toxic pollution to extreme heat, and climate disasters slamming through health systems and infrastructure, the root cause is humanity still burning colossal amounts of coal, oil and gas, and destroying forests,” said Stiell. Data presented by Wellcome Director of Climate and Health, Alan Dangour, underscored the systemic scale of mortality and environmental health disruption: Air Pollution and Thermal Mortality: Combined fossil-fuel air pollution and extreme heat currently claim over 3 million lives each year globally. Agricultural and Sanitation Strain: Extreme drought affected nearly 52% of the world’s land surface for at least one month in 2025—the second-highest level ever recorded—depleting groundwater reserves and disrupting sanitation and food security. Maternal and Newborn Risks: Citing results from a new global survey of 1,000 maternal health professionals, Stiell and Dangour flagged severe physiological threats to pregnant women and newborns caused by extreme thermal exposure. In response, partners at Pre-COP31 in Fiji launched a global call to action to establish medical guidelines, heat response plans, and surveillance data targeting maternal health. The “electric or shock” economic choice To address the structural reforms needed to curb the crisis, the UN Climate Change Executive Secretary gave national delegations a clear economic framing: “electric or shock.” Stiell argued that accelerating clean electrification is both an economic imperative and a primary public health intervention, relieving health budgets and households burdened by volatile fossil-fuel prices. To address chronic underfunding in public health adaptation, philanthropic organisations reported significant progress under the Climate & Health Funders Coalition, originally established at COP30 in Belém with an initial joint commitment of $300 million across more than 35 funding organisations. First-Year Grant Deployments: The coalition has officially awarded over $ 225 million in its first year of operation, supporting targeted interventions in extreme heat management, air pollution reduction, climate-sensitive infectious disease surveillance, and health data systems. Expanded Capital Commitments: Over the past year, the coalition secured an additional $150 million in new financial pledges from existing and incoming donors. Preventative Health Dividends: Global health data indicate that clean air initiatives have already prevented over 300,000 deaths annually across at least 77 countries that reduced fossil-fuel air pollution over the past decade. Despite grim temperature projections, WMO Secretary-General Saulo emphasised that targeted adaptation measures are delivering measurable protections against extreme weather events. A key success has been the rapid global expansion of multi-hazard early warning systems. Secretary-General Saulo stressed that maintaining and extending these life-saving networks requires continuous investment in global meteorological observation networks, warning that decision-makers “cannot afford to fly blind” as climate impacts accelerate. Closing the joint press conference in Antalya, Wellcome Director Alan Dangour called for a fundamental shift in international climate negotiations, urging governments to evaluate policy progress through human health outcomes rather than abstract environmental targets alone. “We must change course and put the health and wellbeing of people at the heart of our response to climate change – measuring success not through emissions targets or degrees Celsius but by lives saved and health outcomes improved. The state of the climate is now, in reality, the biggest indicator of the state of human health,” said Alan Dangour. As COP31 negotiations proceed under the co-guidance of Türkiye and Australia, delegates face growing pressure from international scientific and health bodies to integrate public health protections, clean energy electrification, and dedicated adaptation funding directly into final international agreements.

items.title: Man Utd yet to make decision on Carrick’s future
items.description: Manchester United’s board is yet to make a final decision on Michael Carrick’s future. The 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday means United, 18th in the table, have made their worst domestic start in 40 years. The draw was Carrick’s third match in charge since the board gave the 45-year-old more time to improve the side’s form after a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on 25 October. The board felt Carrick, and the players, had earned the chance to show they could turn the club’s fortunes around, while the hierarchy also knew November’s two-week break would offer a chance to reassess the situation more calmly. They are determined to do exactly that, knowing the results – one win, one draw and one defeat – and performances United have delivered in the past three games offer a mixed view of Carrick’s tenure. Conceding eight goals, winning only once and dropping into the relegation zone are obvious negatives. However, it is also felt that fighting back from two goals down three times over the past two games showed that the players remain behind Carrick. United’s hierarchy explored replacing Carrick after the loss to Bournemouth last month, with ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and former Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann in the mix. Carrick said after the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa that he would not step down, but chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox will influence the decision on whether to keep the former Middlesbrough boss. United travel to arch-rivals Liverpool on 22 November for their first match after the international break, with Carrick’s side in 18th place in the Premier League. With just one league win so far this term, United are in their lowest position in 10 matches since the 1986-87 campaign. Following the Anfield trip, five of United’s next seven league opponents are in the bottom half of the league. This includes the four other sides currently in the bottom five, with meetings against Coventry, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland, all at Old Trafford. Whether Carrick keeps his job or not, United will keep struggling unless they stop conceding goals so regularly. Only Crystal Palace and Ipswich have let in more than United’s 19 league goals. They have conceded 15 times in their last three matches across all competitions. Their only clean sheet this term came against Azerbaijan title winners Sabah FK in the Champions League. ‘Carrick will be puzzled’ “All the Premier League teams, whether they play home or away against Manchester United, fancy their chances because you can open them up and score goals,” former United assistant boss Rene Meulensteen told BBC Radio Five Live. “No matter what combination you find it’s just not good enough. I think Michael Carrick will be constantly puzzled as to what back four he can play because there’s no certainty they can keep a clean sheet.” Full-back Diogo Dalot took the brunt of fan ire at Old Trafford on Sunday. Huge cheers greeted his number being shown to confirm he was being replaced, which then turned to boos when he reached the dugout. Substitute Joshua Zirkzee, who suffered similar treatment when he was replaced after half an hour of a home defeat to Newcastle in December 2024, made a point of hugging Dalot as he made his way back to the bench. Asked if it was time to take Dalot out of the firing line, Carrick urged caution. “We’ve got to be careful with that,” he said. “I understand the frustration and I understand the disappointment of the supporters, I get it. We’re all frustrated, we’re all disappointed, and the players are as much as anyone, I guarantee you that. “Diogo gives absolutely everything. He’s played in different positions and played really well at times. “He gives a penalty away. He knows that. Maybe he can do a little bit better. He made a mistake. But I like what he brings to the team. He cares an awful lot and he’s giving everything.”

items.title: People don’t know full story behind England exile – White
items.description: Arsenal defender Ben White says people don’t know the “full story” behind his earlier decision to make himself unavailable for England selection, but he’d do it again. White, who has been named in Thomas Tuchel’s squad for upcoming Nations League fixtures, left the Three Lions’ camp at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar to return home for personal reasons. He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Gareth Southgate’s reign, and was booed by some fans in March’s 1-1 draw with Ukraine after returning to the squad under Tuchel. Asked by BBC Radio 5 live’s football correspondent John Murray what he would say to people who define his England career by what happened in Qatar, White said: “I think obviously people don’t know the full story, because I [have] never said anything and I won’t put anyone under the bus or share any of that. “I think that is probably the best way. “It’s been amazing [though], obviously a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it is amazing to be here now.” White is now 29 and asked if he would have done anything differently in hindsight, he added: “No, I don’t think I would. “Obviously, I was a bit younger, I am a bit older now. “I think as a person I am quite real and I think I made the decision that I would probably continue to make. “So, one that I am not happy about, but obviously it happened and [it is] time to move on.” White came on for his first England appearance since 2022 in March’s 1-1 draw with Uruguay and was booed by some supporters before he scored but also gave away the penalty that led to the visitors’ equaliser. After that, Chelsea midfielder Jordan Henderson said he and his fellow England players would always support White, while Tuchel said recently that the defender deserves “a new chapter” and “positive feedback from the crowd”. Asked how he dealt with the emotions of that night at Wembley, White added: “Before the game I was thinking ‘don’t not stand out, but [take it] nice and easy’. “Then I came on and obviously got booed, then I scored, then I gave away a penalty. “So, it was obviously full of emotions that night, [but] it was a good night.” England play Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, 12 November, before facing world champions Spain in Madrid three days later. White is looking to add to his six England caps in this international break and said: “It is obviously an amazing privilege to be called up. “The feeling is the same every time you do get this chance to play for England. It’s one I am really looking forward to this week.”

items.title: Habitat et urbanisme : plus de 8,3 MMDH pour les chantiers prioritaires de 2027
items.description: Le ministère de l’Aménagement du territoire, de l’Urbanisme, de l’Habitat et de la Politique de la ville prévoit une enveloppe globale de 8,34 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) pour 2027, incluant le budget général et le Fonds de solidarité pour le logement et l’intégration urbaine. L’accès au logement, l’éradication des bidonvilles, le traitement des bâtiments menaçant ruine et la réduction des disparités territoriales figurent parmi les principaux axes de son programme d’action. Le logement et l’aménagement territorial occupent une place importante dans les priorités budgétaires de 2027. Présentant ce lundi 9 novembre le projet de budget sectoriel devant la Commission de l’intérieur, des collectivités territoriales, de l’habitat, de la politique de la ville et des affaires administratives à la Chambre des représentants, le ministre de tutelle, Samir Belfkih, a annoncé une enveloppe globale de plus de 8,34 MMDH pour financer ces différents programmes. Cette enveloppe comprend 6,24 milliards de dirhams au titre du budget général et 2,1 milliards de dirhams affectés au Fonds de solidarité pour le logement et l’intégration urbaine. Le budget d’investissement s’élève, à lui seul, à 4,84 milliards de dirhams, en progression de 1,97 % par rapport à 2026. Les crédits de fonctionnement consacrés aux dépenses de personnel atteignent 426,05 millions de dirhams, tandis que ceux destinés au matériel et aux dépenses diverses s’établissent à 976,93 millions de dirhams. © Mounir Mehimdate L’aide directe au logement : plus de 127.000 bénéficiaires Le programme d’aide directe au logement reste l’un des principaux dispositifs du département. Au 4 novembre 2026, il avait enregistré 263.840 demandes, dont 237.456 jugées éligibles. Le nombre de bénéficiaires s’élevait à 127.707 depuis son lancement. La répartition des bénéficiaires fait apparaître une présence importante des jeunes et des femmes : 53 % ont moins de 40 ans et 48 % sont des femmes. Les Marocains résidant à l’étranger représentent, pour leur part, 23 % des bénéficiaires. Le ministère entend poursuivre le déploiement du programme 2024-2028, tout en préparant son évaluation et les orientations qui prendront le relais après cette échéance. L’objectif affiché est de faciliter l’accès à un logement abordable et de maintenir des procédures simples pour les demandeurs et les partenaires. En parallèle, le département prévoit de finaliser les contours d’un programme national de logement locatif abordable. Celui-ci doit notamment s’appuyer sur un diagnostic du marché, de l’offre locative disponible et de la demande, ainsi que sur la préparation de son cadre juridique, fiscal et institutionnel. 110.337 ménages concernés par le programme de lutte contre les bidonvilles La lutte contre l’habitat insalubre constitue un autre chantier majeur. Dans le cadre du programme « Villes sans bidonvilles » , 110.337 ménages ont fait l’objet d’engagements contractuels, pour une contribution globale de l’État estimée à 16,53 milliards de dirhams. Les interventions concernent principalement le Grand Casablanca, avec 62.000 ménages ciblés et un financement public de 9,44 milliards de dirhams, ainsi que la préfecture de Marrakech, où 30.000 ménages sont concernés pour une contribution de 4,25 milliards de dirhams. Le programme couvre également la province de Kénitra, avec 12.000 ménages, celle de Benslimane, avec 5.100 ménages, la ville de Safi, avec 500 ménages, et la province de Berkane, avec 737 ménages. Pour la période 2024-2028, le ministère prévoit notamment d'actualiser les listes des bénéficiaires afin de prévenir les doubles inscriptions et les transactions irrégulières, tout en assurant un accompagnement social des familles durant les opérations de relogement. Le dispositif prévoit également une surveillance précoce des constructions illégales dans les communes et les zones périphériques des villes. Le bilan présenté fait état de 392.284 ménages traités depuis le lancement du programme en 2004, soit 76 % des 514.224 ménages recensés. Quelque 121.940 ménages restent concernés par le dispositif, à différents stades d'avancement. © Mounir Mehimdate Bâtiments menaçant ruine : 53.656 ménages pris en charge La sécurisation du parc immobilier constitue également une priorité, notamment dans les zones urbaines anciennes. Les programmes de traitement des bâtiments menaçant ruine affichent un coût global de 8,53 milliards de dirhams, dont 2,54 milliards apportés par le ministère. Sur les 79.434 ménages concernés, 53.656 ont été pris en charge, soit 68 %. En matière de bâti, 27.401 bâtiments ont été traités sur les 43.299 inscrits dans les conventions, correspondant à un taux d'avancement de 63 %. Pour 2027, le département prévoit de poursuivre les interventions à Rabat, de préparer de nouvelles conventions et de généraliser à l’échelle nationale la plateforme numérique BMRPRO, destinée au suivi du traitement des bâtiments concernés. Le programme de renouvellement urbain doit également se poursuivre, avec l’activation des plans déjà conventionnés, la préparation de projets concernant trois quartiers à Casablanca, Safi et Smara, ainsi que la réalisation de trois études préliminaires pour identifier de nouvelles zones susceptibles de bénéficier de ces opérations. Réduire les disparités entre les territoires La politique de la ville et le développement territorial figurent parmi les autres composantes du programme. Le ministère prévoit de poursuivre le programme national de développement intégré des centres ruraux émergents, avec la contractualisation d’une deuxième tranche portant sur 24 centres et concernant 125.565 ménages. Une enveloppe de 1,42 milliard de dirhams est prévue pour ce chantier, dont 457 millions de dirhams à la charge du ministère. Les interventions doivent porter sur les infrastructures, l’accès aux services publics, le développement économique et les questions environnementales. Le département prévoit également de lancer une nouvelle génération de programmes de politique de la ville, fondée sur une cartographie des territoires prioritaires et une programmation intégrée des interventions en milieu urbain et rural. La question du monde rural doit, par ailleurs, faire l’objet d’une conférence nationale précédée de douze rencontres régionales. Cette démarche doit aboutir à une feuille de route intégrant les spécificités territoriales, le logement rural, les centres émergents, les douars et l’économie rurale. © Mounir Mehimdate Urbanisme : 96 documents de planification prévus en 2027 L’accompagnement de l’investissement et la maîtrise de l’expansion urbaine passent également par le renforcement des documents d’urbanisme. Pour 2027, le ministère prévoit l’approbation de six schémas directeurs d’aménagement urbain, de 60 plans d’aménagement, dont neuf dans les grandes villes, ainsi que de 30 plans de développement des groupements d’habitat rural. Le département entend aussi accélérer la mise en place d’outils numériques pour simplifier les procédures et améliorer la gestion territoriale. Le chantier « Taamir 2V » doit notamment permettre de développer un système d’information géographique intégrant les documents d’urbanisme, les cartes d’aptitude à l’urbanisation, les projets de lotissement et l’offre foncière destinée à l’investissement. Le programme prévoit enfin la poursuite de la réforme institutionnelle, avec la mise en place progressive des agences régionales d’urbanisme et d’habitat et la réorganisation des services déconcentrés. À travers ces différents chantiers, le ministère entend articuler politique du logement, planification urbaine et développement territorial. La mise en œuvre des programmes annoncés en 2027 devra notamment répondre à trois enjeux : faciliter l’accès des ménages à un logement abordable, sécuriser les quartiers exposés aux risques et mieux répartir les équipements et les investissements entre les territoires. The post Habitat et urbanisme : plus de 8,3 MMDH pour les chantiers prioritaires de 2027 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

ANOPA Project calls for greater disability inclusion in sports
items.description: The Executive Director of ANOPA Project has called on the government, the Ghana Education Service and other stakeholders to work together to advance disability inclusion in sports in Ghana. He said meaningful inclusion must go beyond giving children with disabilities access to sporting facilities or opportunities to participate. It must also ensure dignity, equity, a sense of belonging and the opportunity to shape the games they play. “Access is not participation, and participation is not necessarily inclusion,” he said. He made the call during a workshop on disability inclusion in sports organised by ANOPA Project in partnership with the RYTHM Foundation on October 28, 2026. The workshop brought together 30 teachers from across the six circuits of the Cape Coast Metropolis. Facilitated by Dr Kwadwo Owusu of the University of Cape Coast, the workshop explored practical ways to adapt sporting activities, equipment and teaching methods to support students with hearing impairments, visual impairments and intellectual disabilities. The training focused on promoting participation and equal opportunities, equipping teachers to create sporting environments where every child feels valued and has a place in the game. The Executive Director emphasised that children with disabilities should have a voice in how sporting activities are designed and delivered. He urged stakeholders to make inclusion a shared priority in school and community sport. ANOPA Project expressed appreciation to the Ghana Education Service, particularly the Metropolitan Physical Education Coordinator, Mr Eric Otoo, and the Special Education Coordinator, Madam Salamatu Gausu, for supporting the initiative. items.title: Lutte contre l’orpaillage clandestin en Guinée : près de 1500 personnes attendues à la barre ce mardi (officiel)
items.description: Le procès de plus de 1000 personnes interpellées dans le cadre de la lutte contre l'orpaillage anarchique est prévu ce mardi 10 novembre 2026, selon le contenu d’un communiqué lu sur la télévision nationale ce lundi 9 novembre 2026. ​Ce communiqué conjoint du ministère de la Défense nationale et du ministère de la Sécurité et de la Protection civile, indique que les suspects ont été mis à la disposition de la justice à l'issue de leurs auditions par les officiers de police judiciaire de la Police nationale et de la Gendarmerie nationale. La note officielle précise également les zones dans lesquelles les opérations se sont déroulées : ​« Les 1 263 personnes interpellées dans la région de Siguiri dans le cadre de la lutte contre l'orpaillage anarchique ont été mises à la disposition de la justice. Leur jugement débute ce mardi 10 novembre 2026. Par ailleurs, les opérations conduites par les forces de défense et de sécurité les 7 et 8 novembre 2026 ont permis l'interpellation de 100 orpailleurs illégaux, de nationalités guinéenne et étrangère, dans la préfecture de Kérouané, ainsi que de 49 autres orpailleurs illégaux dans la zone minière de Siguiri. Ces 149 orpailleurs illégaux interpellés ont également été mis à la disposition de la justice à Kankan, portant ainsi le total cumulé à 1 412 personnes interpellées. » ​Les autorités rassurent l'opinion publique quant au respect strict du cadre légal et des libertés fondamentales : ​« Durant toute la procédure, les intéressés sont traités dans le respect de la loi et des droits humains. La lutte contre l'orpaillage anarchique, préjudiciable à l'environnement, à l'ordre public et au développement durable du pays, se poursuit sur l'ensemble du territoire national afin de préserver les ressources naturelles et de garantir la sécurité des populations. »

items.description: Newcastle’s Dan Burn has joined the England squad to face Croatia and Spain in the Nations League this week after Manchester City defender Marc Guehi pulled out with a hip injury. Guehi was substituted at half-time of City’s loss at Nottingham Forest on Saturday and manager Enzo Maresca said afterwards the centre-back had requested to come off because of the injury. BBC Sport revealed on Sunday that the 26-year-old was having a scan to determine the severity of the ongoing issue, and the defender has now been ruled out of this week’s matches. The former Crystal Palace captain has been a mainstay of Thomas Tuchel’s team since he was appointed England head coach in January 2025. Guehi started in all but one of England’s World Cup games and in all four of the team’s Nations League fixtures in September and October. items.title: I’m a godfather, but I don’t impose appointments on governors — Osoba
items.description: By Efe Onodjae Former Ogun State Governor, Olusegun Osoba has defended the role of political godfathers in Nigeria’s democracy, saying their responsibility should be to offer advice and guidance rather than impose political appointees on elected governors. Osoba, who spoke during a podcast hosted by Reuben Abati and shared on X (formerly Twitter), said he considered himself a political godfather but had deliberately avoided interfering in the administration of his political successors. According to him, he had never nominated anyone for appointment as commissioner, special adviser, councillor or local government chairman in the state. He said: “I agree, I’m a godfather. But one thing that is working for me in my state is that I hardly interfere. I counsel and advise him. I have never nominated one person into his government.” Explaining his position, the former governor said imposing candidates on an administration could undermine the governor’s authority and create unnecessary divisions among his political supporters. He noted that appointing one person from the numerous people around him could offend others, while anyone recommended by him might be viewed with suspicion within the administration. Osoba recalled that during his tenure as governor, he adopted a system that allowed each federal constituency to nominate candidates for commissioner positions. He said he requested one name from each federal constituency and subsequently reviewed their credentials before assigning them portfolios, adding that the approach helped him avoid pressure from political associates. The former governor maintained that political godfathers should ensure that people who worked for a candidate during electioneering campaigns were recognised and compensated, but should not dictate how an elected governor runs his administration. “That’s the role of a godfather. I agree, I’m a godfather,” he said. Osoba also defended the participation of experienced elders in candidate selection, citing his support for a presidential candidate whom he described as experienced, having served in the Lagos State House of Assembly, House of Representatives and Senate, as well as in the corporate sector. The post I’m a godfather, but I don’t impose appointments on governors — Osoba appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Charlie Kirk murder trial set for June 2028, suspect faces death penalty
items.description: The trial of the man accused of murdering US conservative firebrand Charlie Kirk will begin in June 2028, the judge said Monday. “Jury selection will begin June 21, 2028,” judge Tony Graf told the Utah district court, noting that 105 days have been reserved for the trial. Tyler Robinson, 23, faces a potential death penalty for allegedly killing Kirk with a gunshot to the neck on a university campus in the western US state of Utah on September 10, 2025. The killing of Kirk at age 31 at an event planned by his right-wing youth organization, Turning Point, sent shockwaves through the US political world. Kirk had become a popular leader in a Christian Nationalist movement that preaches traditional values while voicing intolerance for diversity and LGBTQ communities. Turning Point was key to mobilizing youth support for Donald Trump’s re-election as president in 2024. The group is now led by his wife, Erika Kirk. The prosecution had sought a trial as early as January 2028, while Robinson’s lawyers had wanted until the end of 2029 to prepare their defense. Last month, Trump criticized the judge and said the case “should be tried within a month, not three years.” Kirk’s assassination last year triggered a 33-hour manhunt culminating in Robinson surrendering to authorities. He has pled not guilty. The prosecution has presented text messages in which Robinson confessed to planning the murder to his roommate, a transgender person with whom they allege Robinson was in a relationship. The defense has focused on alleged weaknesses in the DNA and ballistic evidence. items.title: Kane and Bellingham air strong views in England World Cup review
items.description: England players are understood to have aired strong views about their World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in a team meeting. As BBC Sport reported in September, the Football Association (FA) process included canvassing the opinions of the squad – and it has emerged that took place at a ‘full and frank’ meeting with head coach Thomas Tuchel at the start of the September international break. BBC Sport has been told the squad feel that now they’ve had their say, they can move on from their heartbreak in Atlanta on 15 July. And this was demonstrated in the last international break when England, after a narrow defeat by Spain in the first game, went on to win the next three matches impressively. The ramifications of the Argentina defeat, or perhaps more pertinently, the circumstances, left some in the squad with grievances, and those feelings lingered, even growing, throughout the summer. In particular, there was unhappiness about how Tuchel told them to approach the closing stages of the game after Anthony Gordon had given them a 55th-minute advantage. Enzo Fernandez struck an equaliser with five minutes left, before Lautaro Martinez headed in a stoppage-time winner. As reported by BBC Sport at the time, a number of senior England players held misgivings at Tuchel’s instructions for the closing stages of the Argentina loss, believing the approach was too negative and defensive. Hindsight, of course, is 20/20. England appeared to retreat in the closing stages of the last-16 tie against Mexico earlier in the tournament – but successfully defended a 3-2 lead to reach the quarter-finals to trigger scenes of joy at the iconic Azteca Stadium. Nevertheless, certain players felt let down by the team’s apparent pragmatism during the closing stages of the loss to Argentina amid a sense that going for the South Americans’ jugular would have provided greater success. What was said at the review meeting Inevitably, the game against Argentina emerged as a key theme at the squad discussion. It is understood that Tuchel pointed to the quality of the opposition as a key factor on why they eventually succumbed to two late Argentina goals. There is, of course, merit to that argument. Lionel Messi was in the opposition team after all. That said, it was not an argument the players in the meeting were prepared to universally accept. There is a strongly held view within the England squad that their team, man-for-man, was superior to Argentina, who had 38-year-old Nicolas Otamendi on the field for the closing 18 minutes of the game. All players were afforded an opportunity to air their personal views during the meeting. As you would expect, captain Harry Kane was strong and forthright with his views. Jude Bellingham, too, is said to have been particularly candid in expressing his belief that this current crop of England players were more than capable of continuing to take the game to Argentina. Bellingham’s contribution to the meeting is said to have underlined his growing influence within the England squad, with many believing the Real Madrid midfielder will become the team’s captain once Kane is no longer in the picture. If the air needed to be cleared after the World Cup then it appears those honest discussions at the end of September did the trick. Barring the 3-2 defeat by Spain at Wembley in their first Nations League fixture in September, England have bounced back from the loss to Argentina emphatically – scoring 12 goals without conceding in three fixtures against the Czech Republic and Croatia. Similarly, the fluctuating relationship between Bellingham and Tuchel seems to have improved, too. “It was a bit of an up and down [relationship] of course but we are in a good place,” Tuchel said last week. “I love to be his coach. He’s a top player, a very influential player and I think it goes both ways.” We will get a clearer idea of how ‘Tuchel 2.0’ is progressing in the next few days when England host Croatia on Thursday and travel to Madrid to face world champions Spain on Sunday.

items.title: Musiala may never return to his best – Hoeness
items.description: Bayern Munich forward Jamal Musiala may never “regain the performance level he once had”, says honorary president Uli Hoeness. The 23-year-old Germany international collapsed twice in four days during pre-season, and it was later revealed he had a treatable “neurological dysfunction”. Musiala has scored two goals in four games for Bayern in all competitions this season. “We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,” Hoeness told Bavarian network BR24. Hoeness said Bayern would support Musiala, who is under contract until 2030. Former Bayern and Germany captain Lothar Matthaus said Hoeness is trying to motivate Musiala. “He’s needling him a little. It’s not just about wrapping him in cotton wool. He also has to battle against adversity sometimes,” Matthaus told Sky90. “Uli was looking to create that adversity with this statement. “It’s fine for him to say something like that, because we can’t just put a positive spin on things and somehow wait for him to come back. “If I were in Jamal Musiala’s position, that would be motivation enough to show Uli I’m back.” Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea’s academy. He has scored 71 goals and provided 38 assists in 235 matches for Bayern since breaking into the team as a 17-year-old. One of the youngest Germany players in history, Musiala shared the Golden Boot as the joint leading scorer at Euro 2024. He has not played for Bayern since suffering a hamstring injury in September, but he recently returned to training.

items.title: Le Maroc et l'Équateur déterminés à renforcer leurs relations économiques et commerciales
items.description: Le renforcement des relations économiques et commerciales et le développement des échanges bilatéraux ont été au centre des entretiens, lundi à Rabat, entre le ministre de l’Industrie, du Commerce, de l’Investissement et de l’Inclusion économique, Ryad Mezzour, et le ministre équatorien des Relations extérieures et de la Mobilité humaine, Roberto Carlos Kury Pesantes. S’exprimant à cette occasion, Mezzour a souligné que cette rencontre entre les responsables des deux « pays frères » s’inscrit dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des Hautes Orientations Royales visant à diversifier les partenariats économiques du Royaume. Rappelant la conclusion, cette année, d’un accord de partenariat économique et commercial entre le Maroc et l’Équateur, le ministre a fait savoir que les discussions ont porté sur les moyens de consolider cet accord et de lui donner une portée plus concrète, au service des intérêts des deux pays. De son côté, Kury a indiqué que sa visite au Maroc vise à consolider les relations entre les deux pays et à étudier les possibilités d’investissement et d’accroissement des échanges commerciaux. Les discussions ont également porté sur les opportunités de collaboration dans le domaine de la sécurité, a-t-il ajouté, relevant que le Maroc et l’Équateur, malgré leur éloignement géographique, partagent des défis communs et de nombreuses opportunités. Le ministre équatorien a, en outre, fait état de la volonté de son pays d’examiner les moyens de conclure des accords et d’améliorer les relations commerciales entre les deux pays. Alisson wants to sign new Liverpool contract
items.description: Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker wants to stay at the club beyond the end of the season, when his current contract expires. The 34-year-old joined from Roma for £66.8m in 2018 and has made 347 appearances for the Reds. “Yes [I want to stay], in my mind. I’m focused on playing every game, but in my mind I’m happy to stay,” said Alisson. “That depends on a lot of aspects and different situations. But my will is to stay – I’m happy here, and my family is happy here. “I’m still hungry for titles and to deliver good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can, so that’s my thinking.” Last week, Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said he didn’t know if this would be Alisson’s last season at the club, but hoped the goalkeeper could “continue for more time”. Asked if he has discussed a new deal, Alisson said: “No, but my agent is talking with the club.” The Brazil keeper did consider a move to Juventus earlier this year but ultimately chose to stay at Anfield. After a difficult week, with Liverpool losing to Arsenal and then Fenerbahce , Alisson made several crucial saves in Sunday’s win at Crystal Palace. The goalkeeper says Liverpool now need consistency to challenge for silverware. “Our reality is that we’re not doing as well as we can. It doesn’t mean that we are not doing well – we are doing well in so many games – but the consistency is not there yet,” he said. “We have a top manager, top players. We are capable of great things but as a team we need to get to a point where we feel: ‘We are OK now. We have the confidence. We have everything that’s needed to win.’ “We are building that. I hope we get there really quick but it takes time. “We have to be patient, but as players, in our minds, we don’t have time to waste.”] Analysis: A big call to let Alisson go This is the first time Alisson has discussed his contract this season and, judging by how he spoke after a superb performance at Selhurst Park, he clearly wants to stay at Liverpool . Giorgi Mamardashvili, 26, is waiting in the wings, while highly rated 18-year-old Lucca Brughmans will move to Liverpool from Genk in the summer, so Iraola’s side will not be short of goalkeeping options – but it would be a huge call if they do allow Alisson to leave on a free transfer. His distribution hasn’t been up to the standard we are used to in recent weeks, and Arsenal punished it ruthlessly, but his string of saves against Palace was a timely reminder that he is still a world-class goalkeeper. This season, Liverpool have kept four clean sheets in 10 Premier League games but have conceded 10 goals in four Champions League matches, with Alisson playing every minute in both competitions so far. He is still a leader within the side and was named as one of Iraola’s vice-captains at the start of the season. Alisson did assess his options last season but with senior figures like Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson leaving, he opted to proceed with a one-year extension. With Virgil van Dijk’s contract also set to expire at the end of the season, sporting director Julian Ward faces two major decisions about the future of two men who have been constants for Liverpool since 2018. Of course, both command hefty wages, but this is a young Liverpool side trying to find its way under Iraola, and the head coach will know the value of two experienced players who have been with the club for so long. Perhaps a one-year extension can be offered to Alisson which could allow Brughmans to learn from the Brazilian but, at 34, he may be looking for the security of something longer term. Either way, Liverpool ‘s hierarchy will be watching closely to see how Alisson fares as the season progresses. If he can carry on performing like he did against Palace, then a new contract will be a no-brainer.

items.title: ‎Burkina/Travailleurs de l'informel : « Moins de 10 % bénéficient d'un suivi médical », déplore Dr Chrystel Sanou Ouédraogo, directrice régionale de l'Office de santé des travailleurs (OST)
items.description: ‎Au Burkina Faso, les travailleurs du secteur informel restent largement en marge du suivi médical professionnel, malgré leur prise en compte dans les textes. Selon Dr Chrystel Sanou épouse Ouédraogo, directrice régionale de l'Office de santé des travailleurs (OST), moins de 10 % des actifs de ce secteur bénéficient actuellement d'un suivi. Dans cet entretien, elle indique que parmi les catégories de ce secteur les orpailleurs, les artisans miniers et les travailleurs des carrières sont au premier rang des plus exposés aux maladies du travail. ‎ Lefaso.net : Pouvez-vous nous expliquer le rôle de l'OST dans la protection de la santé au travail au Burkina Faso ? ‎Dr Chrystel Sanou Ouédraogo : La santé au travail est avant tout préventive. Elle ne se limite donc pas aux soins. Cette prévention se décline à trois niveaux. Il y a d'abord la prévention primaire. À ce niveau, nous effectuons des sorties sur le terrain pour aller à la rencontre des travailleurs et observer leurs conditions réelles de travail. Nous appelons ces interventions des visites des lieux de travail. ‎Nous organisons également des séances d'information, d'éducation et de communication au cours desquelles nous échangeons avec les travailleurs. Ces rencontres permettent de les sensibiliser aux bonnes habitudes et aux bonnes pratiques en milieu professionnel, ainsi qu'aux questions de santé, de sécurité et de bien-être au travail. ‎Toujours dans le cadre de la prévention primaire, nous organisons des formations en santé et en sécurité au travail, ainsi que des campagnes de vaccination au profit des travailleurs. Toutes ces actions visent à mieux prévenir les risques auxquels ils sont exposés. Nous avons ensuite la prévention secondaire, qui concerne le suivi médical des travailleurs à travers les visites réglementaires. Il s'agit notamment des visites médicales d'embauche, des visites périodiques, des visites de reprise, des visites spéciales et des visites de fin de contrat. Pour mieux réaliser ces examens, nous les complétons, au besoin, par des examens paracliniques, communément appelés examens complémentaires. Ces visites donnent lieu à la délivrance d'un certificat d'aptitude. Enfin, il y a la prévention tertiaire, qui comprend les consultations curatives, la prise en charge des premiers secours et les soins d'urgence. Au Burkina Faso, 55 maladies professionnelles sont reconnues dans notre tableau des maladies professionnelles. ‎Lorsqu'on parle de santé au travail, on pense généralement aux salariés des entreprises et aux fonctionnaires. Qu'en est-il des travailleurs du secteur informel ? Sont-ils suffisamment pris en compte dans les politiques de prévention ? ‎Je dirais qu'ils sont pris en compte, mais pas suffisamment. Leur prise en compte reste vraiment dérisoire. Le Code du travail prévoit que notre champ d'intervention couvre les travailleurs de tous les secteurs d'activité : le public, le privé structuré, les mines, l'économie informelle et le secteur agro-sylvo-pastoral. Le droit est donc inclusif. Cependant, dans la pratique, les choses sont plus difficiles, d'autant plus que plus de 90 % des actifs exercent dans le secteur informel. Sur cet ensemble, nous en suivons moins de 10 % au niveau de l'OST. La politique nationale existe, mais il y a un décalage entre les textes et la réalité du terrain. La méconnaissance des droits, la dispersion des acteurs du secteur informel et les moyens limités de mise en œuvre expliquent cette faible couverture. Selon Dr Chrystel Sanou épouse Ouédraogo, tout employeur installé au Burkina Faso est tenu d'assurer la couverture sanitaire de ses agents et de ses travailleurs, conformément aux conditions définies ‎Quels sont les principaux risques auxquels les travailleurs du secteur informel sont exposés dans l'exercice de leurs activités ? ‎Il existe plusieurs catégories de risques. Nous avons d'abord les risques chimiques auxquels sont exposés les mécaniciens, les peintres et les coiffeurs. Ils sont notamment en contact avec les hydrocarbures, les solvants et les produits défrisants. Le problème est qu'ils utilisent très peu, voire pas du tout, les équipements de protection individuelle. Nous avons également les risques physiques, particulièrement chez les soudeurs. Il s'agit notamment des rayonnements, de la chaleur, des brûlures et du bruit. Chez les menuisiers, on retrouve aussi l'exposition au bruit et à la poussière de bois. Les vendeurs sur les marchés sont, quant à eux, exposés à la chaleur extrême et à la station debout prolongée. Il existe également des risques biologiques chez les bouchers, les tanneurs, les éleveurs et les personnes qui travaillent dans la récupération des ordures. Ils sont exposés aux zoonoses, aux virus, aux parasitoses et à d'autres pathologies d'origine biologique. Nous avons aussi toute la famille des troubles musculosquelettiques, liés notamment au port de charges chez les dockers, les maçons et dans bien d'autres métiers. Enfin, il y a les risques psychosociaux, liés au stress, à la précarité économique et à l'absence de repos. ‎Parmi ces différentes catégories professionnelles, certaines sont-elles particulièrement vulnérables aux maladies liées à leurs activités ? ‎Au premier rang se trouvent les orpailleurs, les artisans miniers et les travailleurs des carrières qui exercent dans l'informel. Ils sont exposés à plusieurs substances toxiques, notamment le mercure, le cyanure et la silice. Ensuite, viennent les mécaniciens et les soudeurs, qui sont nombreux dans notre pays et travaillent souvent dans des conditions informelles. Ils sont exposés à la surdité, aux atteintes pulmonaires et aux brûlures oculaires, notamment aux kératites. En troisième position, je citerais les teinturières, les coiffeurs et les coiffeuses, qui sont exposés aux dermatoses et à l'asthme en raison des produits chimiques qu'ils utilisent. En quatrième position, nous avons les vendeurs et les restauratrices. Ils travaillent souvent dans la rue, en position debout prolongée ou dans des postures inadaptées. Cela peut entraîner des varices, des lombalgies et des infections respiratoires, souvent liées à la fumée du bois ou du charbon qu'ils utilisent dans leur activité. Enfin, en cinquième position, je citerais les bouchers et les tanneurs, qui sont exposés aux risques de brûlures et aux zoonoses. ‎Un mécanicien qui travaille à son propre compte peut-il bénéficier des prestations de l'OST ou faut-il nécessairement être salarié d'une entreprise affiliée ? ‎Un travailleur indépendant du secteur informel peut tout à fait bénéficier des prestations de l'OST. C'est prévu. Tout employeur installé au Burkina Faso est tenu d'assurer la couverture sanitaire de ses agents et de ses travailleurs, conformément aux conditions définies. Pour un travailleur indépendant exerçant dans l'informel, deux possibilités existent au niveau de l'OST. Il peut d'abord accéder à nos services par une affiliation volontaire individuelle auprès de la direction régionale dont il relève. Dans ce cas, il se déclare comme travailleur indépendant auprès de nos services. Nous disposons de quatre services régionaux, et la personne peut donc s'adresser à la direction compétente pour sa zone. Cette affiliation donne lieu à une cotisation annuelle forfaitaire accessible, qui se situe autour de 15 000 à 25 000 FCFA par an, selon la zone. Elle ouvre droit aux visites médicales périodiques, aux visites des lieux de travail, notamment des ateliers, ainsi qu'aux consultations dans nos services cliniques. La deuxième possibilité consiste à accéder à ces prestations à travers une association professionnelle à laquelle appartient le travailleur, à condition que celle-ci soit affiliée à l'OST. Dans ce cas, ses membres peuvent bénéficier de la couverture. Et le véritable problème reste la méconnaissance de ces dispositions. ‎Disposez-vous de données sur le nombre de travailleurs du secteur informel suivis par l'OST ces dernières années ? ‎Nos statistiques montrent une progression, mais les chiffres restent tout de même très faibles. Actuellement, nous comptons plus de 2 000 entreprises affiliées au niveau national. Cependant, moins de 10 % des travailleurs du secteur informel bénéficient de notre suivi. ‎Pour les années 2023 et 2024, je sais que nous avons pu réaliser environ 800 visites médicales au profit des groupements informels. C'est vraiment dérisoire au regard du nombre d'actifs que compte ce secteur. Mais nous poursuivons nos efforts pour faire mieux. ‎L'OST se rapproche t-elle des lieux d'activité des travailleurs informels pour les sensibiliser ? ‎Oui ! Depuis 2022, nous avons entrepris des campagnes pour aller vers les acteurs du secteur informel. Nous sommes notamment intervenus au grand marché de Ouagadougou, dans des garages, des ateliers de soudure et chez des coiffeuses. Nous organisons également des campagnes gratuites de dépistage de l'hypertension artérielle, du diabète, des troubles visuels et auditifs. Nous faisons aussi des démonstrations sur les Equipements de protection individuelle (EPI). Il s'agit de montrer aux travailleurs quels équipements utiliser en fonction des risques auxquels ils sont exposés, comment les porter et pourquoi il est important de les utiliser. Ces démonstrations se déroulent souvent en langues nationales, parce que nous savons que beaucoup de travailleurs du secteur informel ne sont pas suffisamment alphabétisés. Nous utilisons notamment le mooré et le dioula pour mieux nous faire comprendre. “Un masque qui coûte 500 FCFA ou des lunettes de soudeur à partir de 3 000 FCFA peuvent vous éviter la cécité ou un cancer à 50 ans. Protégez-vous ! Ce n'est pas un luxe”, prévient Dr Sanou ‎Comment se passe l'accompagnement des travailleurs qui développent des maladies liées à leur activité, mais qui ne disposent ni d'un employeur formel ni d'une couverture médicale ? ‎Ce sont des situations vraiment déplorables ! Sans affiliation préalable, il est très difficile pour un travailleur d'obtenir une indemnisation au titre d'une maladie professionnelle. Ce que nous faisons d'abord, c'est diagnostiquer le problème et identifier la maladie. Ensuite, nous orientons la personne vers l'un de nos services cliniques pour approfondir le diagnostic. Dans ces situations, nous établissons un certificat de maladie à caractère professionnel afin de l'aider à constituer un dossier et à rechercher une possibilité d'indemnisation. Nous orientons également les personnes concernées vers la Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale (CNSS), notamment celles qui ont souscrit une cotisation volontaire au régime d'assurance volontaire. Par ailleurs, nous essayons actuellement d'examiner les possibilités de collaboration avec la Caisse nationale d'assurance maladie universelle (CNAMU), dont le dispositif est en cours de déploiement. Nous leur prodiguons aussi des conseils pour aménager ou réaménager leurs postes de travail afin d'éviter l'aggravation de leur maladie. ‎Au regard de ces difficultés, pensez-vous qu'un nouveau cadre réglementaire soit nécessaire pour faciliter la prévention et la prise en charge des travailleurs du secteur informel ? ‎Je dirais que oui, c'est nécessaire ! Le cadre existe déjà et il est bon, mais il est souvent inadapté aux réalités du secteur informel. Il faut donc le rendre plus flexible afin de faciliter l'intégration de la santé au travail dans les activités de ces acteurs. On pourrait, par exemple, faire de la santé et de la sécurité au travail un critère pour l'accès à certains agréments. Il serait également intéressant de créer un carnet de santé du travailleur informel et de renforcer les mesures incitatives plutôt que de privilégier uniquement la répression. Il pourrait s'agir, par exemple, de subventions pour l'acquisition des équipements de protection individuelle au profit des travailleurs affiliés. Toutes ces mesures pourraient les encourager à accorder davantage d'importance à leur suivi médical et à la santé et à la sécurité dans leur environnement de travail. Quelle collaboration l'OST entretient avec les associations professionnelles pour sensibiliser davantage les travailleurs à la santé au travail ? ‎Nous travaillons effectivement avec plusieurs organisations, notamment la Chambre des métiers, la Fédération des associations d'artisans du Burkina, l'UFCB pour les coiffeurs et les coiffeuses, ainsi que les syndicats des bouchers et des tanneurs. Nous collaborons également avec la Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale, l'Inspection médicale du travail et la Direction de la santé et de la sécurité au travail. Ce sont des organisations faîtières qui nous permettent de toucher les acteurs des marchés et des différents ateliers du secteur informel. Ces partenariats facilitent nos interventions auprès des travailleurs. ‎Quelles évolutions souhaiteriez-vous voir intervenir dans les prochaines années pour améliorer la protection sanitaire de ces travailleurs ? Je souhaiterais que, d'ici cinq ans, nous puissions disposer d'une clinique mobile par région, qui s'occuperait exclusivement du secteur informel. Je souhaite également que le régime d'assurance maladie universelle prenne en compte les maladies professionnelles des travailleurs de ce secteur. Il faudrait aussi que chaque apprenti bénéficie d'une formation d'au moins trois jours en santé et sécurité au travail avant de commencer à exercer son métier. A lire : Santé au travail : Dofinihanou « Inessa » Coulibaly, médecin des travailleurs et sentinelle de leur santé ‎Quel message souhaitez-vous adresser aux Burkinabè qui travaillent quotidiennement pour subvenir aux besoins de leurs familles, parfois au détriment de leur propre santé ? ‎Mon message est que ces travailleurs sont des personnes qui se lèvent très tôt, parfois dès 4 heures du matin, pour subvenir aux besoins de leurs familles. Ils se rendent dans les marchés, les garages ou leurs différents ateliers. Je dirais qu'ils sont le moteur du Burkina Faso. Mais sans la santé, il n'y a pas de travail. L'OST n'est pas uniquement destiné aux fonctionnaires, ni seulement aux travailleurs du secteur privé formel. Il est aussi là pour eux, pour tous les citoyens qui travaillent au Burkina Faso, qu'ils relèvent de l'informel ou du formel, du public ou du privé. Un masque qui coûte 500 FCFA ou des lunettes de soudeur à partir de 3 000 FCFA peuvent vous éviter la cécité ou un cancer à 50 ans. Protégez-vous ! Ce n'est pas un luxe, c'est votre premier outil de travail. Les portes de l'OST vous sont grandement ouvertes. ‎Farida Thiombiano ‎Lefaso.net

items.title: Responsible Mining Schemes: Lands minister launches 4 more cooperatives
items.description: The government has stepped up efforts to bring small-scale mining under tighter regulation, with four new mining cooperatives inaugurated in Tarkwa and Bogoso in the Western Region as part of measures to combat illegal mining and create jobs for young people. The cooperatives, two each in the Tarkwa-Nsuaem Municipality and the Prestea-Huni Valley District, were launched on Monday, November 9, 2026, under the Responsible Cooperative Mining and Skills Development Programme (rCOMSDEP). The initiative is expected to provide a structured avenue for community-based mining, improve compliance with mining and environmental regulations and encourage operators to abandon practices that have contributed to the destruction of forests, pollution of water bodies and degradation of farmlands. Launching the schemes, the Minister of Lands and Natural Resources, Mr Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, said the future of the country’s mining industry depended not only on the economic returns from mineral extraction but also on the ability of operators to protect the environment and respect the laws governing the sector. He said the fight against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, required a concerted effort involving government agencies, traditional authorities, mining communities and other stakeholders. Mr Buah described the introduction of the cooperatives in Tarkwa and Bogoso, two of the country’s established mining centres, as an important move towards giving local communities a greater stake in the management of mineral resources. He said the programme was intended to demonstrate that mining could provide sustainable livelihoods without leaving behind destroyed ecosystems and communities struggling with the consequences of environmental degradation. The Minister cautioned that the quest to generate wealth from the country’s mineral deposits should not be allowed to undermine its environmental security. He disclosed that the destruction of forest reserves across the country was equivalent to an area covering more than 12,000 football fields, describing the scale of environmental damage as a serious concern. Mr Buah said the country’s rivers, forests and farmlands must be protected from irresponsible mining, particularly illegal small-scale operations, which continue to pose a threat to livelihoods and the natural environment. He urged mining operators to conduct their activities within the legal and institutional framework, explaining that compliance with mining laws and environmental standards was critical to protecting host communities and building confidence in the sector. He also called for stronger monitoring and cooperation among stakeholders to prevent illegal operators from exploiting weaknesses in the regulatory system. According to him, the success of rCOMSDEP would depend largely on the willingness of mining communities to take ownership of the programme, support lawful operations and reject activities that put their environment and livelihoods at risk. Mr Buah said the government, under President John Dramani Mahama, was committed to managing the country’s mineral resources in a manner that expanded economic opportunities while safeguarding the environment for future generations. He urged the newly inaugurated cooperatives to uphold discipline, transparency and accountability, adding that the programme must translate into measurable improvements in mining practices and the living conditions of host communities. The Acting National Coordinator of rCOMSDEP, Mr Sheihu Siddiq, assured the Minister that the programme would intensify efforts to register more cooperatives to enable them to participate formally in the country’s mining industry. He said expanding the scheme would open up opportunities for young people, create jobs and provide a legitimate pathway for community members to engage in small-scale mining. For his part, the Western Regional Director of the Department of Cooperatives, Mr Akwasi Adjei Bawuah, formally welcomed the new cooperatives and pledged the department’s support to strengthen their operations. He said efforts would be made to streamline their activities and ensure that they operated within the required regulatory framework to help address illegal mining in the region. The Members of Parliament for Tarkwa-Nsuaem and Prestea-Huni Valley, who attended the inauguration, expressed optimism that the programme would improve economic opportunities in their constituencies. They said the cooperatives had the potential to improve the livelihoods of mining communities and provide employment for the growing number of unemployed young people. They urged the beneficiaries to make effective use of the opportunity and ensure that the programme achieved its intended objectives.

Real Madrid legend Raúl named Real Oviedo manager
items.description: Former Real Madrid striker Raul has taken on his first role in senior club management after being appointed, external as boss of Spanish second division side Real Oviedo. The 49-year-old, who coached Real Madrid’s reserves from 2019 to 2025, has signed a contract until June 2028. Raul replaces Julian Calero, who was sacked by Oviedo on Monday with the side ninth in Spain’s second division. “My way of understanding football is with respecting the talent [in the squad] but asking for unconditional effort,” said Raul in a video on Oviedo’s social media. “The team has to fight from the first minute to the last for victory so the fans are proud of them.” Raul enjoyed an illustrious playing career, helping Real Madrid win the Champions League three times and six La Liga titles. He scored 323 goals in 741 games for the Bernabeu side before going on to play for Germany’s Schalke, Al Sadd in Qatar, and American club New York Cosmos. On the international front, Raul managed 44 goals in 102 games for Spain.

items.title: Poundland unable to buy new stock as fears over collapse grow
items.description: Poundland can’t buy new stock to restock its shelves after its owners blocked access to cash in its bank accounts. The discount chain is on the brink of collapse, with one insider describing it as “running on fumes”. It has until Thursday to secure a rescue deal. Its American owner, Gordon Brothers, has frozen about £ 50 m, the BBC understands, leaving its 600 shops running out of stock. Pressure is building on Gordon Brothers, which bought Poundland for £1 last June, after the owner rejected a takeover bid that could have saved the thousands of jobs currently at risk. Gordon Brothers has been approached for comment. Poundland has filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators, which protects it from its creditors until Thursday. Access to funds was limited because of tension over Gordon Brothers’ dual role as both creditor and shareholder, a source said, but added they expected funds to ease in the next two days. Last week, Poundland boss Barry Williams said like-for-like sales, excluding new store openings, were up 11.4% last week, including Halloween, and that this was £1.5m ahead of budget. He said the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a “strong recovery” from the previous year where the business made losses of £68m. The latest annual accounts have not yet been audited. However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture of the business, saying the chain remains “challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading”. It said it had provided significant funding to support the company’s ability to trade since it acquired the business. It has also made £18m, from a combination of debt interest payments and other fees and charges. On Wednesday, executives from Gordon Brothers will appear before the Business Select Committee with MPs probing whether they are genuinely pursuing a solvent rescue of the business, which has 11,000 employees, and whether every realistic step is being taken to protect jobs and stores. The session is being held in private given commercially sensitive discussions are still under way with bidders. Uncertain future On Thursday, the 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended. If not, Poundland is set to collapse into administration and could be broken up. A source familiar with the sales process said London-based Xyra Group was making “significant progress” in its last minute bid to buy Poundland and could now be the front runner. An extension of Thursday’s deadline now seems an increasingly likely scenario. But such a case would be difficult to put forward if Gordon Brothers continues to block funding. One observer remarked “if Gordon Brothers is going in front of that committee, you don’t want to be giving the message we’re pulling up the drawbridge”. Even if a deal is agreed to sell the business as a whole, there is no guarantee a new owner would not reduce the number of stores, but suppliers to Poundland would prefer that outcome to hundreds of sites being sold off to other retailers. There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up stores which could mean continuing employment for many workers. The central issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland trading as a national chain.
