items.title: How to Talk to Your Child About the Cybertruck’s Demise
items.description: Join Alexandra Petri for a live Q&A on Tuesday, November 10, at 11 a.m. ET at theatlantic.com . Sit down with your child in a quiet place. He or she may have many questions, such as, “Those big silver trucks that looked like a kid drew them , they are not making them anymore?” and “But if there are no Cybertrucks anymore, how will I know whom not to date when I grow up?” Be warm and calm. Explain that the trucks were in pain, and had been in pain for a long time, because their bodies were not properly designed for the job they were doing. Explain that they are not going to a farm upstate, because they would be unable to deal with the terrain there. Explain that, yes, these were supposed to be the trucks of the future. But then people took a look at that future and said, “No. Bring us another future, please.” Use short words, pausing frequently. Sometimes basic concepts can be difficult to grasp, especially if you have a strong, incorrect idea in your head already. This unfortunate fact explains much of the design of the Cybertruck. A simple script can be best. Say something like, A truck is a special kind of vehicle for carrying large loads. Some trucks are big rigs. Some trucks are tow trucks. Some trucks are abominations in the eyes of God and Man and should never have been brought into existence. This truck was the third kind of truck, and people didn’t like that . I know the car looked cool, like a refrigerator that was trying to puff itself up to intimidate a predator. But people prefer it when their wheels don’t fall off. Actually, it is not “normal” or “cool” for the wheels to fall off , and anyone who tries to tell you otherwise is mistaken . No, not all trucks like to drink gasoline. That was not what was wrong with the truck. What was wrong with the truck was everything else . If you want to, take time to explain. Usually, stainless steel does not rust . Usually, a truck’s doors respond to your commands . Usually, trucks have brakes that work . Explain that the Cybertruck would be driving off into the sunset, but its wheels have fallen off, so it will sit there into the sunset instead. Explain that you don’t know what the Cybercab is either, and it is okay not to know. Tell your child not to worry. All of the other Monster Trucks are still okay. And if your child asks, “Was the truck bad?” Be honest. Say yes.

items.title: Public Notice To Gaming Operators And The General Public.
items.description: FEDERAL CAPITAL TERRITORY LOTTERY REGULATORY OFFICE (FCT-LRO) O ﬃ ce of the Director-General PUBLIC NOTICE TO GAMING OPERATORS AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC. FCT-LRO COMMENCES FULL BUSINESS OPERATIONS The Federal Capital Territory Lottery Regulatory Oﬃce (FCT-LRO) hereby informs gaming operators, industry stakeholders and the general public that the Oﬃce has commenced operations as the regulatory authority responsible for the oversight, regulation and supervision of gaming activities within the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). 1. REGULATORY JURISDICTION Following the Supreme Court judgment in Attorney-General of Lagos State & 21 Others v. Attorney-General of the Federation & 15 Others, Suit No. SC/1/2008, the constitutional position on the regulation of lotteries and gaming has been clarified. By virtue of Section 299 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended), the FCT has a distinct constitutional status, with the National Assembly exercising legislative powers ordinarily vested in a State House of Assembly. Accordingly, gaming operators conducting business within the FCT are required to comply with the applicable FCT licensing and regulatory requirements and engage with the FCT- LRO on all regulatory matters. 2. ONLINE GAMING OPERATIONS The Oﬃce clarifies that the Supreme Court judgment did not expressly settle the full regulatory framework applicable to online gaming. In particular, the judgment did not establish that any one State has exclusive regulatory control over the online gaming market. Accordingly, the online gaming market remains open to operators and investors. Operators are free to choose the regulator from whom they wish to obtain their gaming licence or authorisation, based on their business model, operational needs and the regulatory framework they consider most suitable and beneficial to their business. This choice may be exercised without undue interference, intimidation or coercive treatment by any State regulator solely on the basis that an operator has elected to obtain its licence from another regulator, as every state is duly empowered to regulate gaming activities within its relevant jurisdiction. Operators are, however, reminded that the online nature of a gaming platform does not, in itself, exempt an operation from applicable licensing and regulatory obligations where such obligations arise. The FCT-LRO remains committed to providing a transparent, consistent and predictable regulatory environment for digital gaming operations within the Federal Capital Territory. 3. NOTICE TO FORMER NLRC LICENSEES All gaming operators previously licensed by the National Lottery Regulatory Commission (NLRC) who are currently operating, or intend to operate, within the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) are hereby required to approach the FCT-LRO to regularise their regulatory status. The Oﬃce further clarifies that any NLRC licence that remains valid and has not expired will be recognised for the remainder of its validity period and converted to the corresponding FCT-LRO licence. Accordingly, holders of former NLRC licences will retain the benefit of their unexpired licence terms, subject to the regularisation process prescribed by the FCT-LRO. Aﬀected operators are required to present and hand over their former NLRC-issued licences for verification and documentation, complete the applicable regularisation procedures and obtain the appropriate FCT gaming licence. All aﬀected operators are required to commence the regularisation process within 7 days of publication of this notice. 4. Telephone: +234 802 347 6076 / +234 813 052 5876 Email: info@lro.abj.gov.ng The FCT-LRO reiterates its commitment to promoting responsible gaming, protecting consumers, strengthening regulatory oversight and fostering a transparent and investment- friendly gaming industry within the Federal Capital Territory. items.title: Polémiques en France : Bagayoko qualifie la bataille de Poitiers de «mythe» et de «folklore»
items.description: « Poitiers, la ville qui aurait degage les Arabes ». Lors d'une prise de parole, a l'occasion d'un meeting organise a Poitiers le 30 octobre, Bally Bagayoko s'est en pris a l'une des dates cle du recit national francais : la bataille de Poitiers, au cours de laquelle le maire du palais Charles Martel a defait une armee venue d'al-Andalus et au cours de laquelle le chef omeyyade, Abd al-Rahman, est tue. « Ils ont fait d'une bataille vieille de treize siecles un etendard, une frontiere imaginaire entre eux et nous », a poursuivi le maire La France insoumise de Saint-Denis. « D'abord ce mythe, ce n'est pas un folklore innocent », a-t-il ajoute, avant de renvoyer a l'occupation en 2012 du chantier de la mosquee de la ville par des militants de Generation identitaire – au cours de laquelle des banderoles renvoyant a la bataille de Poitiers avaient ete deployees – et de dresser un parallele avec l'attentat terroriste de Christchurch, en Nouvelle-Zelande, en 2019. Un attentat au cours duquel 51 personnes ont ete assassinees, dans deux mosquees, et ou l'inscription « Tours 732 » – nom de la bataille en anglais – figurait sur l'une des armes employees. « Vous voyez bien la concomitance parfaite entre ces deux evenements. Voila ou menent ces mythes : de la provocation au massacre », a insiste Bally Bagayoko. « Poitiers n'appartient pas a leur fantasme », a-t-il ajoute, avant d'accoler une lecture contemporaine en decrivant « une ville universitaire, une ville jeune, une ville ou des etudiantes et des etudiants venus de toute la France et du monde entier apprennent, travaillent, construisent leur vie ». Cet edile LFI n'en est pas a son coup d'essai en matiere de polemiques depuis son election. Le maire de la ville des rois et reines de France, comme il aime a le repeter, a indigne un large spectre de la classe politique francaise lorsqu'en juin il avait estime legitime de siffler l'hymne national lors de matchs de football. Acte qui, selon lui, pouvait representer « un droit a la replique populaire » lorsque « la France se deshonore par ses actes a l'international ». Meme chose lorsque, plus recemment, a l'occasion d'une interview parue dans la presse espagnole sur fond de grogne lyceenne, il avait accuse la police francaise de « violences disproportionnees » ainsi que de racisme.

items.title: Cameroun : le président Paul Biya convoque le corps électoral pour les élections municipales et législatives 2027
items.description: © DR Le décret du président de la république rendu public ce lundi 09 novembre 2026 convoque les citoyens camerounais inscrits sur les listes électorales à aller aux urnes le dimanche 07 février 2027. C’est certain. Sauf cas de force majeur, les élections municipales et législatives se tiendront le 07 février 2027. La certitude découle d’un décret signé du président de la République Paul Biya et rendu public ce lundi. D’après le texte, le corps électoral est convoqué le dimanche 07 février 2027 à l’effet de précéder à l’élection des conseillers municipaux et des députés. Le même texte précise que les bureaux de vote ouvriront à 08h et se refermeront à 18h le jour du vote. Déjà attendu depuis quelques semaines, le décret convoquant le corps électoral arrive dans un environnement déjà en préparation des prochaines élections. Les états-majors des partis politiques sont en ordre de bataille sur le terrain. Ils mènent des opérations de sensibilisation et de mobilisation des militants. Ils procèdent aux installations des responsables des démembrements locaux. Ils tiennent tour à tour des conventions ou congrès pour régulariser certaines situations. Tout comme des partis politiques mènent des négociations pour former des coalitions. Le décret présidentiel qui fixe la date des élections vient ainsi accélérer les activités préélectorales sur le terrain. Ces dernières vont concerner les investitures des listes de candidatures aussi bien pour les élections locales que pour les législatives. Ces investitures vont précéder le dépôt et la validation de ces candidatures, puis la campagne électorale et l’élection. C’est ainsi parti pour un processus électoral venant mettre un terme au mandat prorogé deux fois de suite des conseillers municipaux et des députés. Cet article Cameroun : le président Paul Biya convoque le corps électoral pour les élections municipales et législatives 2027 est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Trois médailles remportées aux JOJ Dakar 2026 : l’Indonésie célèbre une performance
items.description: Avec trois médailles, dont une en argent et deux en bronze, l’Indonésie signe une « performance historique » aux Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. L’exploit a été célébré vendredi dernier par l’ambassade, en présence de la « team » Indonésie. 3 médailles dont une en argent et deux en bronze. Une performance « historique » qui a été célébrée, le vendredi 6 novembre 2026, par l’ambassade de l’Indonésie à Dakar. La médaille d’argent a été remportée par l’athlète Asael Christo Jacob Rondonuwu en Wushu et les deux en bronze par Sashenka Cahaya Fatim en judo et Michelle Surjadi Fang en natation. Les 18 athlètes et leurs encadreurs ont été conviés à une réception dans la luxueuse résidence de l’ambassadeur, Ardian Wicaksono. La cérémonie a été également marquée par la présence d’Antoine Wardini, présenté comme « un ami de l’Indonésie ». Dans une atmosphère de convivialité, les membres de la délégation et leurs différents invités ont partagé ce moment de célébration. A lire aussi : Coopération décentralisée : Dakar et Jakarta jettent les bases d’un jumelage Selon l’ambassadeur, Ardian Wicaksono, cette performance des jeunes athlètes indonésiens constitue un encouragement pour la relève sportive indonésienne. « Le Sénégal est un pays très particulier, très spécial. Le but de ces Jeux olympiques est de construire un pont pour la diplomatie des sports entre le Sénégal et l’Indonésie », a plaidé l’ambassadeur. La cheffe de mission de la délégation indonésienne, Ita Yutali, a salué la prouesse des athlètes indonésiens. Une « belle récompense » qui, à son avis, témoigne du potentiel des Indonésiens. Ces médailles, dit-elle, ouvrent de nouvelles perspectives pour le développement du sport en Indonésie. Dans son intervention, Antoine Wardini a rappelé que le Sénégal et l’Indonésie partagent « plusieurs valeurs profondes », à savoir l’amour de leur jeunesse, le travail, la terre et l’hospitalité. « Ces Joj ne doivent pas seulement être une compétition, mais une passerelle entre les deux peuples ; un brassage culturel qui va tisser des souvenirs éternels », a indiqué M. Wardini. La cérémonie a été clôturée par une remise de cadeaux aux membres de la délégation indonésienne, à l’ambassadeur de l’Indonésie à Dakar et à Antoine Wardini. Aliou Ngamby NDIAYE

items.title: 2027: NDC will provide all-inclusive government – Kwankwaso
items.description: By Henry Umoru Ahead of January 16 2027 election, the Vice Presidential Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has promised Nigerians that an NDC-led Federal Government under Peter Obi and himself will operate an all-inclusive government. According to him, the Obi-led government would prioritise the interests of every Nigerian, irrespective of political, ethnic, religious or social affiliations. The former Kano State Governor spoke while addressing party leaders, stakeholders and supporters during a carnival-like reception organised in his honour at Toru-Orua, the country home of Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, National Leader of the NDC and the party’s Senatorial candidate for Bayelsa West. In a statement signed by the Coordinator, Ofurumapepe Media of the NDC Campaign Council, Gabriel Ukuta, he explained that Kwankwaso said that what Nigeria needed at this moment in the nation’s political history is a government that would deliberately carry its citizens along in the formulation, implementation of policies and programmes. He said that governance must be people-oriented and responsive to the needs and aspirations of the population. Kwankwaso said the NDC has positioned itself as a credible alternative political platform with the capacity, leadership and commitment to deliver the inclusive governance Nigerians desire. The NDC Vice Presidential Candidate said, “Nigerians deserve a government that will listen to them, accommodate their interests and ensure that no section of the country is left behind. An NDC-led Federal Government will be an all-inclusive government that will carry everybody along in its policies and programmes,” Kwankwaso who condemned what he described as the prevailing hunger, economic hardship and insecurity under the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led Federal Government, urged Nigerians to take advantage of the 2027 general elections to vote out the ruling party. The Vice Presidential Candidate who called on citizens to take collective responsibility for the electoral process by coming out en masse to vote for the NDC and ensuring that their votes count, expressed concern over alleged attempts by anti-democracy forces and agents of the ruling party to manipulate the outcome of the forthcoming elections, insisting that Nigerians must remain vigilant and protect their votes. “Voting is not enough; Nigerians must also take responsibility for protecting their votes. We must all work together to ensure that the wishes of the people are respected and that the outcome of the elections reflects the collective decision of the electorate,” he added. He expressed appreciation to Senator Dickson, members of the NDC National Working Committee (NWC), the National Campaign Council (NCC), party stakeholders, candidates and supporters across Bayelsa State for the impressive reception accorded him. In his remarks, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, who is also the NDC candidate for Bayelsa West Senatorial District, decried what he described as the growing hardship, hunger, insecurity, victimisation, inducement and intimidation allegedly being experienced by the people of Bayelsa State under the APC-led Federal and State Governments. Dickson maintained that the NDC presidential and vice-presidential candidates were tested and trustworthy leaders with the requisite experience, competence and commitment to restore good governance and bring the dividends of democracy to the doorsteps of Nigerians. He expressed confidence in the Obi-Kwankwaso ticket, describing both candidates as individuals capable of providing purposeful leadership and addressing the country’s numerous socio-economic challenges. The former Bayelsa State governor urged Bayelsans to return to their various communities and intensify mobilisation for the NDC, emphasising the need for collective support for all the party’s candidates, from the presidential election to the State House of Assembly polls. He called on party faithful and supporters to sustain the momentum generated by the reception and translate it into grassroots political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. Dickson also thanked the dignitaries, party leaders, candidates, stakeholders and supporters who attended the event, expressing his appreciation in the Ijaw language and reaffirming the inclusive character of the NDC. He declared that the NDC was a political platform for all Bayelsans and Nigerians, irrespective of their backgrounds or previous political affiliations. The statement further said, ” A major highlight of the reception was the participation of Engineer Kwankwaso in the traditional Ijaw war boat display, popularly known as Ama-Aru, alongside Senator Dickson and other NDC leaders and executives in Bayelsa State, all of whom were led to the even by the party’s National Chairman, Sen. Moses Cleopas. “The colourful cultural display, which took place along the Toru-Orua axis of the River Forcados, showcased the rich cultural heritage and traditional identity of the Ijaw people. “The event also featured the formal presentation of party flags to the NDC candidates contesting the National Assembly and State House of Assembly elections in Bayelsa State, signalling the party’s readiness for the 2027 electoral contest.” Vanguard News The post 2027: NDC will provide all-inclusive government – Kwankwaso appeared first on Vanguard News .

Hajj 2027 : Le Sénégal signe un protocole d’accord avec l’Arabie saoudite
items.description: Le Délégué général au pèlerinage aux Lieux saints de l’islam, le général de division (2S) Mamadou Gaye, a signé, lundi à Djeddah, au nom de l’État du Sénégal, le protocole d’accord avec le Royaume d’Arabie saoudite définissant les modalités d’organisation du Hajj 2027, a appris le Soleil. La signature est intervenue à l’issue d’une audience accordée à la délégation sénégalaise par le vice-ministre saoudien du Hajj et de la Oumra, Dr Abdulfattah bin Suleiman Al Mashat, en marge de la sixième Conférence et Exposition du Hajj (Hajj Confex) 2026. Le protocole signé par les deux autorités fixe les obligations respectives des parties, notamment en matière d’accueil, de transport, d’hébergement, ainsi que les exigences sanitaires et administratives applicables aux pèlerins sénégalais. Au cours de la rencontre, le responsable saoudien a salué l’engagement et les dispositions anticipatives de la Délégation générale au pèlerinage (DGP) dans la préparation de l’édition 2027 du Hajj. Il a également magnifié les efforts consentis par les autorités sénégalaises pour assurer une bonne préparation du prochain pèlerinage. En retour, le général Mamadou Gaye a exprimé, au nom de l’État du Sénégal, sa gratitude au Royaume d’Arabie saoudite pour son accompagnement et son soutien, qui contribuent à garantir aux pèlerins sénégalais de meilleures conditions de confort et de sécurité. La délégation sénégalaise comprenait également le premier délégué général adjoint, Assane Ndiaye, le délégué général adjoint chargé des voyagistes privés et de la communication, coordonnateur de l’initiative « Tariq Makka », Mohamed Mansour Ndiaye, ainsi que l’ambassadeur Cheikh Abdou Ndiaye, secrétaire permanent de la DGP. La rencontre s’est déroulée en présence de hauts responsables du ministère saoudien du Hajj et de la Oumra. La sixième Conférence et Exposition du Hajj constitue une plateforme internationale annuelle organisée par le ministère saoudien du Hajj et de la Oumra, en partenariat avec le Programme de services aux pèlerins. Elle vise notamment à améliorer la prise en charge des fidèles, à favoriser le partage d’expériences et de connaissances et à renforcer la coopération entre les acteurs du secteur. S.G

items.description: Dans le cadre des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse Dakar 2026, le Centre culturel régional de Thiès, en collaboration avec le Cojoj et le projet Dundal Joj, lance à partir de ce mardi le programme des Plateaux, un volet artistique de « Thiès, ville olympique des arts ». Dans un communiqué de presse, le centre culturel régional de Thiès propose, du 6 au 13 novembre 2026, onze rendez-vous de musique, de théâtre, d’humour, de danse, de conte et de slam, dans les quartiers de la ville, à Mont Rolland et dans d’autres communes du département de Thiès. Ce programme dénommé « Thiès, ville olympique des arts », c’est aussi sept sessions d’ateliers de création artistique pour les enfants et douze journées de Fan-Zone qui complètent le dispositif. Selon le texte, « les Plateaux ont été construits dans un esprit de déconcentration de toute la programmation en plusieurs endroits de la ville, pour aller à la rencontre du public jusque dans les places publiques, les quartiers et les communes ». A lire aussi : Keur Serigne Abdoulaye Yakhine de Thiès: quartier historique, pôle d’aspirations Ainsi, au cours de ces onze rendez-vous, « les disciplines se relaient d’un lieu à l’autre à travers la musique traditionnelle et le hip-hop qui ouvrent et referment la séquence, le théâtre circule en région, la danse et le conte prennent les places publiques. » Avec le Centre culturel, « Thiès devient la ville olympique des arts, un statut et un label engagés pour accompagner les Joj, à travers la création sénégalaise qui doit être visible, accessible et partagée, faisant des habitants les premiers spectateurs de ce qui se joue chez eux ». items.title: An Electoral Mess in Mississippi
items.description: L ast summer, Mississippi began an effort to “continue to build on the accuracy of Mississippi’s voter rolls and strengthen the integrity of elections,” as Republican Secretary of State Michael Watson put it. Using data from the credit-reporting agency Experian, the state scrutinized its list of registered voters, searching for anyone who may have moved, left the state, or died. Tens of thousands of Mississippians had their active registrations shifted to inactive—a crucial step toward purging them from the rolls. On Tuesday, many of those inactive voters showed up at the polls, only to be told that they were not properly registered. Their best option was to fill out an affidavit ballot, a more involved process that increases the likelihood that a vote will not count. Now a Senate seat is on the line, and the Democratic challenger, Scott Colom, leads the Republican incumbent, Cindy Hyde-Smith, by just about 2,500 ballots. And voting-rights advocates say that Mississippi, a state with a long history of voter suppression and discrimination, has once again undermined one of its citizens’ most sacred rights. Experian now says that its data were never supposed to be used to scrub Mississippi’s voter rolls in this way. Watson said in a social-media post that the inconvenience of having to fill out an affidavit ballot was “well worth the election integrity added by having cleaner voter rolls!” A postelection legal battle over the affidavit ballots is intensifying, as lawyers from the campaigns and voting-rights groups argue over how those ballots should be treated. Hyde-Smith’s campaign has called for affidavit ballots to be separated from regular ballots, suggesting that it may attempt to challenge their validity in the days ahead. Colom’s campaign has said there is no legal basis for treating affidavit ballots any differently once they are processed. The back-and-forth could be a precursor to a legal battle in which the courts could ultimately decide whether Colom or Hyde-Smith prevails. The situation is already drawing comparisons to Mississippi’s past efforts to systematically disenfranchise Black voters. In DeSoto County, inactivations surged in recent months, and the number of active voters declined by nearly 10,000 from September to October, according to state data. The county, just south of Memphis, is home to one of Mississippi’s largest concentrations of Black voters. A 2025 review of Experian’s voter-roll-maintenance data by the U.S. Election Assistance Commission, the bipartisan federal agency that supports election administration, found that zip codes with higher proportions of Black residents were more likely to be flagged for “new addresses,” potentially leading to voter inactivations. Because Experian has a national database that can be used to surface evidence that a person may have moved to a new address, officials in a handful of states have turned to it, and other similar commercial sources, to try to keep their voter rolls up-to-date. Some election officials used the data to contact voters and encourage them to update their voter registrations, or to send postcards to a subset of voters they’d had trouble reaching. But Mississippi used the data far more aggressively. Scott Anderson, Experian’s vice president for corporate communications, told us that the company has not provided services to Mississippi since early 2025. “The solution provided at that time consisted of supplemental address information and was not designed or intended to validate voter records.” Mississippi plowed ahead, despite warnings that the data were error-prone and could introduce far more problems than they solved, multiple officials and voting-rights advocates told us. One of those officials, Jim Hood, a Democrat who served as Mississippi’s attorney general from 2004 to 2020, sued Experian in 2014 over errors in its credit reports, eventually settling with the company and two other credit-reporting bureaus for $7.2 million. “I’d be leery of doing any business with them, especially on something as sensitive as somebody’s constitutional right to vote,” he told us. Hood said that his daughter was among those told on Tuesday that she was not an active voter, despite showing up at the same precinct she has always gone to. She ended up having to fill out an affidavit ballot. Just how many other Mississippians showed up to vote only to learn that they had been inactivated is unclear. Some advocates on both sides of the contest estimated last week that 10,000 to 25,000 affidavit ballots remained uncounted, a number that could easily swing the race. Half a dozen voters who’d had to fill out affidavit ballots told us that they are unsure their votes will count; the state says that nearly a quarter of these ballots are being rejected. Watson said in a statement last week that his office had received “multiple calls” about inactive voters on Election Day, but he seemed to downplay the impact. “Voter roll maintenance is the cornerstone of election integrity,” he wrote on X. He has since assured Mississippians that every legal vote will be counted, calling the affidavit-ballot process a “safety net for errors.” Our emails and calls to his office and cellphone went unanswered. I f there was one thing Virginia Gordon-Lang’s mother had taught her, it was how to vote. The 38-year-old recounted to us the times her mom took her hand as they walked into a church or school to cast a ballot. On Election Day this year, however, she showed up to three different locations, attempting to vote for Colom. She didn’t appear on the rosters of eligible voters at any of the locations, she said. When she finally made it to the front of the line at the last precinct, Gordon-Lang said, a poll worker told her that she was not on the active-voter list. Gordon-Lang, a Marine Corps veteran who had moved in April, said that she told the worker that she had filled out required paperwork weeks ago confirming her home address, and that she had never missed an election. She filled out an affidavit ballot. Gordon-Lang said that a Hinds County election official had called a few days after the election to tell her that she was no longer a registered voter and that her ballot was going to be thrown out. (Hinds County officials did not respond to our phone calls.) After spending 15 years on active duty—including time in Iraq, Afghanistan, and Germany—Gordon-Lang was devastated. “It’s like a slap in the face,” she said. “That’s what makes me so angry.” She contacted the Meridian Lauderdale County NAACP branch, which is trying to make sure that all eligible votes are tallied. “I want my vote to count,” she told us. “I want my vote back—that’s what I want.” [ Read: The arc of the Voting Rights Act ] Whether Gordon-Lang represents a singular case or a broader trend could determine the ultimate outcome of one of the most watched races in the country. Voting-rights groups, attorneys, and campaign staff are fanning out across the state, gathering stories of people who may have been wrongly turned away or made to cast a ballot provisionally through the affidavit process. They are also holed up watching the county-by-county process determine which votes will be counted. As of this afternoon, Mississippi reported that 14,239 affidavit ballots had been processed, and 23 percent of them had been rejected. Civil-rights groups that sent Watson a letter a few days before the election, warning about the unreliability of Experian data, say that rightful voters have now been limited in their ability to cast a ballot. “It shows how antiquated and broken our system is,” Amir Badat, the southern-states director and senior director of Fair Fight Action, a national voting-rights organization based in Georgia, told us. “This is what modern-day voter suppression looks like.” Representatives from several groups told us stories about ballots being rejected because poll workers—not voters—failed to adhere to strict procedures that required them to sign affidavits, and stories about voters whose registration should not have been affected but were somehow categorized as inactive. Tonya Rivers, a Rankin County election commissioner, told us that commissioners were urgently trying to verify “questionable” data from Experian as it processes affidavit ballots. “I want clean voter rolls just as much as anybody,” she said. “But cleaning up voter rolls shouldn’t mean creating problems for legitimate voters in the process.” Although most states and counties rely primarily on government data to maintain and update their voter lists, some states have begun to use private credit-reporting data as well. But not everyone is using it as Mississippi has. The West Virginia secretary of state’s office participated in a federal pilot program with Experian but opted to use the company’s data in a far more limited way than Mississippi did, officials there told us. They analyzed data from the company’s True Trace program specifically to identify about 15,860 voters who may have moved without updating their voter registration. “Postcards were mailed to the folks identified only through Experian data, but we did not inactivate any nonresponding voters or place them in a queue for future cancellation,” West Virginia’s deputy secretary of state, Donald Kersey III, told us in an email. “It was used only as outreach.” West Virginia decided not to continue using Experian after the pilot, officials there told us, citing costs and other factors. El Paso County, Colorado, also used the data to reach out to voters rather than automatically inactivating them, County Clerk Steve Schleiker told us. Mississippi, by contrast, used Experian’s data to run 1.9 million checks of voters’ data, roughly equivalent to the state’s total number of active registered voters, allowing county officials to begin a process that culminated in thousands of people being shifted to “inactive” status. An April report in Mississippi Today found that at least 50,000 voters had been inactivated over address issues from July 2025 to March 2026. Those changes were made even though Experian told Mississippi, in disclaimers in an initial contract, that it could not guarantee that its data were accurate, and local officials warned the state that the credit agency was prone to reporting inaccurate addresses, the report said. The outlet reported last Monday that by the time of Tuesday’s election, the list of inactive voters had surged to 230,000, accounting for about one in nine of the state’s registered voters. Some of them supported Hyde-Smith. Michelle Pratt, a Republican, was told that her name wasn’t on the voting list when she tried to cast a ballot at a church near her home in Meridian. She said a poll worker asked whether she had moved recently; she has lived in the same home for eight years. Pratt voted by affidavit ballot for Hyde-Smith and said the experience left her suspicious about the process: “It makes you wonder: How do I know if my vote was counted—you know, mine or anybody’s?” D e’Angelo Houston, the president of the Meridian Lauderdale County NAACP branch, told us that he and other observers are gathering information from people who had not moved over the past decade, yet were told on Election Day that their registration was not active. He said last week that observers were watching as Lauderdale County election commissioners sifted through piles of affidavit ballots to either reject or accept them. “We are documenting the reasons why they are refusing,” he said. Houston said he watched as one election official rejected 21 affidavit ballots for missing signatures, either from the voter or a poll worker. In DeSoto County on Friday, observers from the Democratic Party were watching through a window as election officials determined, precinct by precinct, which affidavit ballots would be accepted and which would be rejected. Every now and then, officials gave updates to observers about how many affidavit ballots were rejected, and why, Deborah Williams, the chair of the DeSoto County Democratic Executive Committee, told us. She said that a lot of voters “are going to end up being disenfranchised.” The Mississippi secretary of state’s office told the local-news outlet 16 WAPT last month that it no longer uses Experian’s data and is now contracting with a different commercial company, IDI Data, to help maintain its voter rolls. The state has been experimenting with options for maintaining its voter list in recent years but has not joined a bipartisan, multistate compact that shares information about voters. Spurred by conspiracy theories suggesting that the nonprofit Electronic Registration Information Center was part of a left-wing plot, a number of Republican-led states ditched the group in 2023. [ Read: The election deniers’ long game ] Former Georgia Deputy Secretary of State Gabriel Sterling told us that commercial data can be useful for voter-roll maintenance “if it’s part of a broader ecosystem of data you’re working with.” But he cautioned against efforts to deactivate voters based on potentially flawed data that are not corroborated, and he criticized Mississippi’s rule requiring voters who show up with valid identification to fill out an affidavit ballot if they are not on the active-voters list. In Georgia and other states, inactive voters can fill out a normal ballot—and be automatically reactivated—if they show up at a voting precinct with appropriate identification. There is good reason for states such as Mississippi to keep a close eye on their voter rolls. Federal and state data indicate that people regularly move or change their name without updating their voter registration. Watson, the Mississippi secretary of state, has pointed out that in at least three counties, the population of registered voters is larger than the estimated number of citizens older than 18. But there is little evidence of the kind of voter fraud that would justify the mass purges of voter rolls that Republicans aligned with President Trump support. Hood told us that during his 16 years as attorney general, and eight years as a district attorney prior to that, he hunted for true evidence of widespread voter fraud—and always came up short. The idea that fraudsters would go through the trouble of trying to vote using registrations of people who have died or left Mississippi—a state without early in-person voting and with limited voting by mail—is detached from reality, he said. “We have a system that works, and they’re just looking for a problem to fix that’s not there,” Hood said. “It’s not a lot of people going in there voting that are not legit. The problem is getting people to go vote that are legit.” As the country awaits the results of what may be the most narrowly decided Senate contest in decades in Mississippi, Americans are also seeing the fallout of experimenting with unreliable tools to satisfy the ever-evolving demands of election activists.

items.title: Trump's 'Board of Peace' says Israel too slow as floods ravage Gaza
items.description: United States President Donald Trump’s “Board of Peace” said on Monday that Israel needed to act immediately to help war-battered Gaza cope with impending winter, saying measures ahead of deadly floods had been insufficient. “The situation no longer represents simply a threat posed by the approaching winter, but an immediate humanitarian emergency,” the Board of Peace said in a statement. Heavy rain over the past two days has swept away tens of thousands of tents in the territory, where virtually the entire population has been displaced at least once, and killed at least five people, according to authorities in Gaza. The Board of Peace, tasked with implementation of an October 2025 US-brokered ceasefire announced between Israel and Hamas, said it had been warning Israel, which controls all entry into the territory, of the need to prepare both for the winter and seasonal flooding. Moments before the statement came out, the Israeli military claimed it had allowed more than 8,200 trucks to enter the Gaza Strip with supplies including 91,000 tents. The Board of Peace acknowledged steps Israel said it took but noted that they remain “insufficient”. “We call on the leadership of the current Government of Israel to act immediately to authorise and facilitate the entry of all necessary winterisation and humanitarian supplies,” it said. Israel has taken a biting tone against Hamas over the floods, saying the group should have invested in infrastructure instead of weaponry. “Hamas doesn’t get to escape responsibility every time it rains,” the Israeli foreign ministry posted on Sunday on X. The Board of Peace also called on Hamas to abide by commitments under the ceasefire. Despite the truce, Israel has kept up nearly daily strikes in Gaza. Israel’s relentless campaign prior to the so-called ceasefire killed over 74,000 Palestinians and has left it increasingly isolated on the world stage, with Amnesty International , Human Rights Watch and experts declaring its actions in Gaza as a “genocide”, which Tel Aviv rejects. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is fighting for his political survival following tight elections last month, has vowed to kill anyone involved in Hamas’s Oct 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest day ever for Israel.

items.title: Turkiye steel factory blast kills 16; probe launched
items.description: An explosion ripped through a steel plant in western Turkiye on Monday, killing 16 people and injuring 13, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said, announcing investigations into the tragedy. Eight workers were trapped at the HABAS steel factory about 60 kilometres north of the port city of Izmir, where the blast struck around midday (2pm PKT), governor Suleyman Elban said. Footage posted online showed a huge cloud of thick smoke pouring into the sky as flames appeared to engulf a tall structure within the HABAS Demir Celik plant in Aliaga. “The circumstances surrounding this tragic incident, which has deeply saddened our nation, including how and why it happened, whether there was any negligence and who bears responsibility, will be established,” Erdogan said on television, adding that two of the injured were in serious condition. HABAS is a privately owned group and one of Turkiye’s top steel producers. Crane collapse According to Izmir’s governor, the blast was caused by an overhead crane that collapsed into a large industrial furnace used during the liquid steel casting process. “While a boiler replacement operation was being carried out at the HABAS iron and steel factory, the overhead crane fell and landed in the arc furnace, causing an explosion in the steel mill behind it,” Elban told reporters, referring to a large electric-powered steelmaking furnace. Workers walk after an explosion at an iron and steel manufacturing plant in the Aliaga district of Turkiye’s coastal Izmir province on November 9, 2026. — Reuters An eyewitness, Deniz Ulker, said it felt like an “earthquake”. “When I looked at the factory across the street, thick black smoke was coming out. A fire broke out where the chimney was,” Ulker told Anadolu news agency. “It was like a bomb going off,” said Turan Ilbay, who works as a truck driver at the factory and also spoke to Anadolu . Izmir mayor Cemil Tugay said on X that rescue teams were “continuing their work to remove the collapsed platform” and that those affected were factory workers. Safety issues Workers’ groups said there was a long record of safety issues at HABAS. Contacted by an AFP journalist, HABAS declined to answer questions. Before Monday’s explosion, the Evrensel daily said at least 11 workers had died over the past decade while working there. Turkiye’s Labour Party, a small Marxist faction, said on X it was the third time in three weeks that workers had lost their lives at HABAS. It said one man died after falling eight metres from a ladder on Oct 21, while another died when a tyre he was inflating on a construction machine exploded. Outside the hospital where the injured were taken, two representatives of the leftist Aegean Workers’ Collective were arrested while trying to make a statement about workplace safety issues, a group spokesman said. “The HABAS management’s blind greed for profit has resulted in a major disaster today,” their spokesman Oktay Turk told AFP . “Those responsible for this massacre must be brought to justice,” he said, calling for the immediate release of his colleagues. The pro-Kurdish DEM party, in a statement, called the disaster “unacceptable”. “The causes of the explosion, any possible negligence and lack of oversight must be revealed transparently, and no one responsible must go unpunished.”

items.title: UK man convicted of fraud for secretly working five government jobs at once
items.description: A 56-year-old civil servant in the United Kingdom, UK, Kashim Chowdhury has been convicted of nine counts of fraud after secretly holding multiple full-time government jobs and fraudulently earning more than £284,000 in taxpayers’ money. Chowdhury, from east London, held five overlapping government positions in the spring of 2023, concealing his multiple employment arrangements from the departments that hired him. After seven hours of deliberation, a jury unanimously found him guilty of eight counts of fraud by false representation and one count of fraud by failure to disclose. The prosecution accused Chowdhury of “deliberate, intentional dishonesty” and “exploiting the system” to secure multiple salaries from public sector employers. During the proceedings, the judge said Chowdhury faced a “very significant custodial sentence”. He also refused him bail, citing the seriousness of the offences and Chowdhury’s own wellbeing. Sarah Melo, a specialist prosecutor at the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) Serious Economic Organised Crime and International Directorate, described his actions as sustained dishonesty. “This was sustained and deliberate dishonesty,” Melo said. “He knew he could not legitimately hold multiple full-time positions at the same time, but continued to conceal what he was doing.” A spokesperson for the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said Chowdhury had “abused the trust placed in him as a public servant”. The department added that it would use all available avenues to recover the proceeds of his offending. Between 2020 and 2023, Chowdhury held eight overlapping full-time public sector positions and earned a total of £350,000, according to evidence presented in court. Prosecutors told the court that he provided inaccurate information about his employment status on job application forms and failed to disclose to government departments that he was already employed as a civil servant. After securing the positions, he also failed to inform his employers that he was working for other government departments. Chowdhury was permitted to work entirely from home after telling his employers he was caring for his mother, with whom he lived in east London. His mother had dementia and was diagnosed with terminal cancer in 2023. However, rather than reduce his workload to care for her, he continued taking on additional government positions. In the spring of 2023, he held positions across the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs, the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office. During the period, he was contracted to work 183 hours a week, exceeding the total number of hours available in seven days.
